questions.q: In this lab's scenario, what does the Equipment Checkout team want that a plain Update Set move from Dev to Test wouldn't give them?
options: Real code review — an actual pull request, read and approved by a teammate before merging
A faster way to delete old Update Sets
A way to avoid using Studio entirely
A way to skip connecting the application to any repository
questions.explain: The scenario's whole point is adding a genuine review step, which an Update Set move alone doesn't provide.

questions.q: Why does the developer build the due-date reminder feature on its own feature branch instead of editing the main line directly?
options: To isolate this one piece of work from whatever else the rest of the team might be changing in Dev at the same time
Because Studio does not allow editing the main line under any circumstances
Because feature branches are required by ServiceNow licensing
Because a feature branch automatically deploys to Production
questions.explain: A feature branch keeps one developer's in-progress work separate from the shared codebase until it's ready.

questions.q: What actually happens when the developer opens a pull request against the application's main branch?
options: A teammate reads the real diff of what changed, can leave comments, and approves only once satisfied
The change is immediately and automatically merged with no review
The feature branch is deleted without being reviewed
The Test instance is updated before any review occurs
questions.explain: The pull request is the review gate: a teammate reads the diff, comments, and approves before anything merges.

questions.q: In what order does the change actually move, according to this lab's worked scenario?
options: Branch and push the feature, open a pull request, get it reviewed and merged, then pull the merged change into Test
Pull into Test first, then open a pull request afterward
Merge into main before the feature branch is ever pushed
Skip the pull request and push directly from Dev into Production
questions.explain: The sequence is: branch and push the feature, open the PR, review and merge, then pull the approved change into Test.

questions.q: Why does the lesson connect this workflow to Chapter 4's Automated Test Framework?
options: A reviewed, traceable change sitting in Test is exactly the kind of change ATF is built to verify automatically going forward
ATF replaces the need for pull requests entirely
ATF can only test changes that were never reviewed by a teammate
Chapter 4 has no real connection to anything covered in this lab
questions.explain: Source control makes the change trustworthy and traceable enough to be worth testing automatically — which is exactly what Chapter 4 picks up next.
